home.subtitle: Here you can strengthen and reinforce your memory by practicing a few simple challenges.

card.title: Random irregulars
card.description: Do you know the three forms of the most common irregular verbs? Put yourself to the test. I'll give you the verb's infinitive (base form) as a hint, and you take it from there. Or you can turn on 'Expert mode', where I'll give you any of the three verb forms as a hint, and you'll complete the trio from there.

fillGapsCard.title: Fill in the gaps
fillGapsCard.description: Prefer to see them in context? We'll show you real sentences with a gap where the verb should be, and you type in the correct form. We mix all three verb forms — infinitive, simple past, and participle — across different sentences, so you practice the exact spelling of each one.

crosswordCard.title: Crossword
crosswordCard.description: Do you like classic challenges? Solve a crossword made of irregular verbs: each word has an English definition as a clue, and crossing words share letters with each other.

voices.title: About the pronunciation voices
voices.intro: The voices you hear for each verb tense (and for the examples) depend largely on the voices installed on your operating system. This app uses your browser's own speech synthesizer, so the more voices — and the better their quality — you have installed on your device, the more natural the pronunciation will sound.
voices.outro: Below is a quick guide to installing more natural voices ("Enhanced", "Premium", or neural voices) on each operating system. After installing them, restart your browser so it can detect them.

windows.title: Windows
steps: Open Settings → Time & Language → Speech (or Settings → Accessibility → Narrator, depending on the version).
Search for "English (United Kingdom)" and "English (United States)" and install the available voices.
On Windows 11, some voices are labeled "Natural": these are the highest-quality ones, generated with neural networks.
Restart your browser so it picks up the newly installed voices.

macos.title: macOS
steps: Open System Settings → Accessibility → Spoken Content (on older versions: System Preferences → Accessibility → Speech).
Click the "System voice" dropdown and choose "Manage Voices...".

Look for English voices and download the ones marked "Enhanced" or "Premium" (for example, Serena or Zoe for British/American English): they use much more natural synthesis than the default compact voices.
Quit and reopen your browser after the download finishes.

linux.title: Linux
steps: On Linux, system voices usually rely on speech-dispatcher together with an engine such as espeak-ng or Festival, which sound fairly robotic by default.

The easiest way to get a natural pronunciation is to use Google Chrome: when there's an internet connection, Chrome offers Google's "network" voices (for example, "Google UK English Female"), which sound much better.
If you prefer offline voices, you can install an alternative engine such as RHVoice from your distribution's package manager and set it as the default voice in speech-dispatcher.

ios.title: iOS / iPadOS
steps: Open Settings → Accessibility → Spoken Content → Voices.
Choose "English" and select the accent you prefer (United Kingdom or United States).
Tap the voice you want and download the "Enhanced" or "Premium" quality (a download icon appears; it requires Wi-Fi and some storage space).

android.title: Android
steps: Open Settings → System → Languages & input → Text-to-speech output (the path may vary by manufacturer; on some devices it's under Settings → Accessibility).
Make sure the "Preferred engine" is "Google Text-to-speech Engine", which usually comes preinstalled.
Tap the gear icon next to the Google engine, go to "Install voice data", and download the highest-quality English voice pack available.
If no high-quality voices show up, update the "Google Text-to-speech" app from the Play Store.
